_comment: Where the free addon is supposed to send someone who wants to pay.
LocGuard Lite is free for exactly one commercial reason: it sits inside the
user's editor and hands them to LocGuard Pro ($12). The whole conversion
path is ONE node — the promo LinkButton at the bottom of the dock — and its
destination lived only as a string literal inside plugin.gd, checked by
nothing. verify.sh's `funnel` stage is about something else entirely: it
keeps Lite a strict SUBSET of Pro (don't give the $12 rules away). A Lite
that reports exactly the free rules and sends nobody anywhere passes every
one of the six original stages.
Committed here so test_upsell_lite.gd compares the SHIPPED addon against a
contract instead of against the same literal it is testing.
paid_url is the destination; paid_game_id is the itch game it must be.
free_repo_url is deliberately listed too: it is the FREE open-source CLI,
one letter away from the paid page in the README, and a promo aimed there
would look perfectly healthy while costing every sale.
cta_identity_text must be the LEADING words of the button label: the dock
clips long labels, so whatever comes after it may never be read.
narrow_dock_width_px is the conservative right-dock width we require the
CTA to survive (the real editor at 1280x720 gives it ~450px).
